Maintaining the 5.25–5.50% target range while noting a “lack of further progress” toward 2% is a hawkish hold aimed at preserving anti-inflation credibility, consistent with time-inconsistency and inflation-bias insights (Barro–Gordon) and with rule-of-thumb prescriptions like the Taylor rule when inflation is above target. The shift to “better balance” of risks reflects flexible inflation targeting and forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford, 2005), while the emphasis on expectations and vigilance aligns with New Keynesian Phillips curve dynamics (Galí). Slowing QT by cutting the monthly Treasury redemption cap from $60B to $25B modestly eases balance-sheet restraint via the term-structure channel (in line with evidence that long-term rates and the yield-curve slope affect and are considered by the Fed; Cochrane–Piazzesi). Net tone: growth-positive and inflation-vigilant, with a slightly dovish nuance on the balance sheet—overall near-neutral.
